clue.text: Singer's second note in series of 1 down 5?

parts.note: Sting is the singer, formerly of the Police; the 's links the pieces
in tonic sol-fa, doh ray me, the second note is ray (also spelt re)

explanation.surface: A question about which note a singer hits second in some series.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 down 5 reads SUPERMARIO + NATION, i.e. supermarionation, the puppet technique of Gerry Anderson's TV shows.
explanation.definitionFit: Stingray was a 1960s Gerry Anderson puppet adventure series filmed in supermarionation.

clue.text: 3 might move him — with name, he could fly to next Olympics?

definitions.text: 3 might move him — with name, he could fly to next Olympics?

parts.words: 3 might move him — with name, he could fly to next Olympics?
parts.note: a gamer (3 down) steers this Nintendo plumber; Japan's prime minister appeared dressed as him at the Rio closing ceremony to hand over to Tokyo, and adding N for name links this light to 5 across

explanation.surface: A riddle about a figure a player controls who might fly to the next Olympic Games.
explanation.walkthrough: Shinzo Abe emerged as the Nintendo hero at the Rio 2016 closing ceremony. 'With name' adds N, so this light runs on into 5 across to name Gerry Anderson's puppet technique.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nintendo plumber is moved around the screen by whoever holds the controller, and starred in Japan's Olympic handover.

clue.text: Caffeine reduced in treatment during cold — lack of capacity to work

indicators.note: one piece sits within the other, the treated letters coming during the word for cold

parts.note: icy means very cold

indicators.note: letters undergoing treatment are worked over and rearranged
reduced means cut down, here losing its final letter E

explanation.surface: A drug lowered during treatment for a cold leaves a patient unable to function.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' cuts CAFFEINE to CAFFEIN; 'in treatment' rearranges that to NEFFICA, which goes 'during' ICY.
explanation.definitionFit: Inefficacy is a failure to produce the intended effect, an inability to do the job.

clue.text: Golf in the morning, let me see one playing

parts.note: G is Golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a.m. means in the morning
er is the hesitant sound someone makes while thinking, like 'let me see'

explanation.surface: Someone recalling a morning round of golf while watching a person at play.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamer is a person who plays games, especially video games.

clue.text: American series on hospital department initially leaving you in a severe way

parts.note: a string is a series of things in a row
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

indicators.note: initially means the opening letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: A US television series about a hospital department departs harshly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' here just places one piece after another.
explanation.definitionFit: Astringent can mean harsh or severe, so the adverb describes acting sternly.

clue.text: Close to Gordon Brown in recession — No 10 dividing country

indicators.note: dividing means splitting the reversed letters by sitting in the middle of them
recession means going backwards, so the letters are read in reverse
close to means the final letter of the word Gordon

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour
the number 10 is written as the figures 1 and 0, read as the letters I and O

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown, near the end of his tenure, at Number 10 during a recession, splitting the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in recession' turns the last letter of Gordon plus the colour round; 'dividing' puts the figures of 10, read as letters, inside. Gordon Brown was UK prime minister, living at No 10 Downing Street.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation is a country, a people under one government.

clue.text: They shorten game in topless bars

indicators.note: in places the game inside the shortened word
topless means the first letter, the top of the word bars, is removed

parts.note: bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: Sounds like a card game played in establishments with topless staff.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to shorten it, so abridgers are people who condense.

clue.text: Fish catcher? Source of the runs around India

indicators.note: around means the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: IBS, irritable bowel syndrome, is a cause of diarrhoea, colloquially 'the runs'
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Two separate ideas: a fish catcher, and the cause of an Indian stomach upset.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibis is a wading bird that catches fish and other small water creatures.

clue.text: Kitchen, Rope, Miss Scarlet — finally a set that fits together

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of each of these words is taken

explanation.surface: A Cluedo accusation: in the kitchen, with the rope, Miss Scarlet, the case finally solved.
explanation.walkthrough: Cluedo is a board game where players name a room, weapon and suspect; Miss Scarlet, the rope and the kitchen are all in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest of tables or boxes is a set of graduated items that slot inside one another.

clue.text: Secures in advance unfinished press boxes, mostly vacant

indicators.note: boxes means encloses, holding the other piece inside
unfinished means the word press loses its final letter
mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: vacant means empty

explanation.surface: Someone preparing ahead by boxing up a part-built press that stands mostly empty.
explanation.definitionFit: To pre-empt is to act first and so secure something before anyone else can.

clue.text: Rings of gold chunks

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
bits are pieces or chunks

explanation.surface: Jewellery made of lumps of gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Orbits are circular paths round a body, so they are rings in a loose sense.

clue.text: Burnt dish — red after cooking show that used 1 down 5?

indicators.note: cooking means the letters are mixed up as if in a recipe

explanation.surface: A dish that has gone red after being burnt, and a show featuring it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after cooking' tells the solver to stir the three surface words together; the dish is a red herring. 1 down 5 is supermarionation, Gerry Anderson's puppet-filming technique.
explanation.definitionFit: Thunderbirds was Gerry Anderson's best-known puppet series, made in supermarionation.

clue.text: Once more supplied grass without John's partner

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the grass goes round the other piece

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
David Furnish is the husband of Elton John

explanation.surface: Grass growing with no sign of John's other half.
explanation.definitionFit: To refurnish is to supply with furniture again, so the past tense means furnished anew.

clue.text: This puts it bluntly, one left Mac to play with Sonic

indicators.note: to play with means the letters are toyed with and moved around

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone abandoning their Mac to play a Sonic the Hedgehog game, put bluntly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just joins the last fodder word; the anagram is of I, L, MAC and SONIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Laconicism is terse, blunt brevity of speech, named after the curt Spartans of Laconia.

clue.text: Writer to stuff in names of magical figures

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

indicators.note: in places the stuffing inside the names

parts.note: tags are names or labels
to ram is to stuff or cram

explanation.surface: A writer cramming names into a book of spells.
explanation.definitionFit: Pentagrams are five-pointed stars used as symbols in magic.

clue.text: Copper imprisons idiot (on the contrary) in enlarged cell

indicators.note: imprisons means one piece holds the other inside it
on the contrary reverses the stated roles, so the idiot surrounds the copper

parts.note: an ass is a fool
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A policeman locking up a fool in an oversized cell.
explanation.walkthrough: Read straight, CU would hold ASS; 'on the contrary' swaps that so ASS holds CU.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascus is the enlarged sac-like cell in which certain fungi form their spores.

clue.text: Charming Spanish golfer interrupted by Channel 1

indicators.note: interrupted by means the other pieces break into the golfer's name

parts.note: Seve Ballesteros was the famous Spanish golfer
a duct is a channel or tube
1 is written as I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A charming Spanish golfer's round broken off by a TV channel.
explanation.definitionFit: Seductive means alluring or tempting, close in sense to charming.

clue.text: Drink and drink, cocktail of lager and last bit of wine

parts.note: gin is an alcoholic drink

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters are mixed
last bit of means the final letter of wine

explanation.surface: Ordering drink after drink, including a mix of lager and wine dregs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail of' mixes LAGER with E, the 'last bit of' wine, into GERALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginger ale is a fizzy soft drink flavoured with ginger.

clue.text: Rate current police coppers: no pressure

parts.note: in means fashionable or current
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of the British police

indicators.note: no means the letter for pressure is taken out

parts.note: coppers are small coins, pennies, so pence
P is the symbol for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: Measuring how often current police officers work without pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coppers' looks like more police, but means copper coins, PENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Incidence is the rate at which something happens, as in the incidence of a disease.

clue.text: Characters in 11 make footballer

definitions.meaning: two people in Thunderbirds: ... Tracy, pilot of Thunderbird 1
the England midfielder who played for Chelsea, West Ham and Spurs

explanation.walkthrough: 11 down is the puppet show; 'make' just joins the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Joining the two puppet names gives the full name of an English midfielder.

clue.text: Clubs excite Beatle — Ringo's not old and is at party …

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

indicators.note: to excite is to stir up, so the letters are stirred into a new order
not means the letter for old is removed

parts.note: Ringo Starr was the Beatles' drummer; the 's means 'is'

explanation.surface: A Beatles fan thrilled that Ringo still feels young and is at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excite' stirs BEATLE and RING (Ringo with no O) together; 'and is' links, and the ellipsis leads into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone at a party is out celebrating, marking an occasion with festivities.

clue.text: Fireball cast? Unusual end from creator of 1 down 5?

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken away from the creator's name

parts.note: Gerry Anderson created the supermarionation puppet shows
the letters of the word end in an unusual order, giving a scrambled form of it

explanation.surface: A question about the cast of a fiery show and a strange end for its creator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual end' makes NDE, which comes out of ANDERSON. Fireball XL5 was another Anderson series, but here a cast fireball is a deliberate fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Casting a fireball deliberately sets something alight, which is the crime of arson.

clue.text: Hands over in trade

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: paws is slang for hands

explanation.surface: Someone handing goods across as part of a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: To swap is to exchange one thing for another, which is what a trade is.

clue.text: Poet Virgil's last letter to head

indicators.note: last letter means the final letter of the poet's name is taken

parts.note: an ear is the head of a cereal plant such as corn

explanation.surface: A note on how the Roman poet Virgil's last letter reached its addressee's head.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Lear was the English nonsense poet. 'Virgil' tempts as the definition; it only supplies L.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Lear was a Victorian writer of nonsense verse and limericks.

clue.text: … Beatle, on Radio 6 — go live outside

indicators.note: outside means the first pieces sit around the number

parts.note: to wee, to go to the toilet, is informal for urinate
L marks the live terminal on an electric plug
VI is 6 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A Beatle appearing on BBC Radio 6 Music for a live outside broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beatle, on Radio' sounds like beetle, which the answer is; the ellipsis carries on from the Beatle in 20.
explanation.definitionFit: A weevil is a kind of beetle, and the word said out loud matches the band name.

clue.text: Plant one in 11 in leaves, so given Alan's tip

indicators.note: leaves means the word in departs from the character's name

parts.note: Brains is the scientist in Thunderbirds
sic, Latin for thus or so, marks a quotation as written

indicators.note: tip means the first letter of Alan's

explanation.surface: A plant in a show, one in the leaves, given a pointer by Alan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in leaves' looks like foliage but means IN is removed. Alan Tracy is also a Thunderbirds character.
explanation.definitionFit: Brassica is the genus of plants including cabbage, mustard and sprouts.

clue.text: See 19
He doesn't appear in tabloid writer's main dangers

indicators.note: doesn't appear in means these letters are left out of the paper's name

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
Kingsley or Martin Amis, British novelists; the 's links

explanation.surface: A man absent from a tabloid writer's column about big threats.
explanation.definitionFit: Tsunamis are giant sea waves, so they are dangers of the main, an old word for the sea.
